question: A communications team wants to start using a Claude capability on client-facing work, and believes the company's written AI standard may not address it. The standard itself says that anything it does not cover needs the policy owner's position before anyone uses it, even on internal material. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) Check whether the standard covers the capability at all; ask the policy owner to give a position on the capability; pilot the capability on internal material only; roll it out to client work and record the agreed position in the standard.

B) Ask the policy owner to give a position on the capability; check whether the standard covers the capability at all; pilot the capability on internal material only; roll it out to client work and record the agreed position in the standard.

C) Pilot the capability on internal material only; check whether the standard covers the capability at all; ask the policy owner to give a position on the capability; roll it out to client work and record the agreed position in the standard.

D) Check whether the standard covers the capability at all; pilot the capability on internal material only; ask the policy owner to give a position on the capability; roll it out to client work and record the agreed position in the standard.
correct_answers: A) Check whether the standard covers the capability at all; ask the policy owner to give a position on the capability; pilot the capability on internal material only; roll it out to client work and record the agreed position in the standard.
explanations: Correct. Reading the standard establishes whether there is a gap at all; only a real gap justifies asking the policy owner for a position, which the standard requires before any use; an internal pilot then tests the capability where a mistake stays inside the company; and updating the standard makes the decision durable for everyone else.

The policy owner is asked to rule before anyone has checked whether the existing standard already covers the capability, which wastes an escalation and risks a new position that contradicts the written rules. Asking is only needed for something the standard leaves uncovered.

Use begins before anyone has even opened the standard, and before the policy owner has said anything, which breaks the standard's own rule and is the sequence that produces shadow adoption and leaves governance to catch up afterwards.

The pilot starts before the policy owner has given a position, but the standard requires that position before anyone uses an uncovered capability, even on internal material. Keeping the pilot on lower-stakes material does not make it sanctioned.
